Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The NCRA operates a centralized ID Verification System that provides digital authentication via API or portal. Verification is read-only, consent-driven (biometrics or OTP), transparent, and auditable. Banks, telecom operators, and other institutions connect via API to authenticate identities against the NCRA database. The blockchain-based digital identity platform (2019, with Kiva) and MOSIP pilot (2024) further confirm digital authentication capability.
revision_notes: Fetched all three cited sources. The two ID4Africa AGM presentations (2023, 2024) confirm a centralised, API/portal-based ID Verification System that is read-only, consent-driven and auditable, supporting Yes=2. The third cited NCRA blockchain announcement page returned a 403 error and could not be verified directly, but is not needed as the ID4Africa material independently confirms the score. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: The National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA) operates a centralised, API- and portal-based ID Verification System that enables digital authentication of identities. Verification is read-only, consent-driven (via biometrics or OTP) and auditable. Banks, telecom operators and other institutions connect to the system via API to authenticate identities against the national database, as confirmed in NCRA presentations to the ID4Africa AGM in 2023 and 2024.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The NIN is required for access to government services including NASSIT (national social security), NRA (tax), SLRSA (driving licenses), immigration services, public sector employment, and educational enrollment. The NCRA's verification portal is used by government agencies. The ID4Africa 2023 and 2024 presentations show the NIN 'is at the centre of Sierra Leone's Digital Public Infrastructure (eGov)' and links to consular, tax, passport, and pension services.
revision_notes: Fetched cited sources. ID4Africa 2024 presentation confirms a centralised ID Verification System accessible 'by API or Portal', and states the NIN 'is at the centre of Sierra Leone's Digital Public Infrastructure (eGov)', linking to NASSIT, NRA, SLRSA, immigration and other services. Forumnews-sl (Dec 2024) confirms a wide range of services requiring NIN/ID verification from 2025. The 2023 ID4Africa PDF was also checked and supports the same picture. Evidence supports a centralised government verification portal rather than a distinct citizen-facing SSO portal, but this meets the variable definition. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Authentication against the National Identification Number (NIN) is available through the NCRA's centralised ID Verification System, accessible via API or portal, which underpins access to a wide range of government services including social security (NASSIT), tax (NRA), driver licensing (SLRSA), immigration, education and public sector employment. The NIN sits at the centre of Sierra Leone's digital government service architecture.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Electronic KYC (eKYC) is explicitly enabled through the NCRA's ID verification platform. President Bio stated at the 2023 eID card launch: 'banks, forex bureaus, micro-finance institutions, mobile money providers, and other financial service providers can now easily and effectively carry out the electronic know-your-customer (eKYC) process.' Commercial banks signed MOUs with NCRA for identity verification and eKYC; API-based NIN verification supports KYC compliance. Smile ID, Uqudo and other third parties also offer NIN-based KYC verification services in Sierra Leone.
revision_notes: Fetched all cited sources. WeAreTech.Africa (Feb 2023) quotes President Bio explicitly confirming eKYC is enabled via the chip-based biometric ID for banks, forex bureaus, microfinance institutions and mobile money providers. Third-party identity verification vendors Smile ID and Uqudo both offer NIN/national ID-based eKYC verification services for Sierra Leone, corroborating live eKYC enablement. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Electronic Know-Your-Customer (eKYC) verification is enabled through the NCRA's identity platform. Banks, forex bureaus, microfinance institutions and mobile money providers can carry out eKYC checks against the national ID database, and third-party verification providers such as Smile ID and Uqudo offer NIN-based KYC/AML verification services for the Sierra Leonean market.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Sierra Leone has a general judiciary and rule-of-law system that can adjudicate disputes related to identity and civil registration under the NCR Act 2016. The Right to Access Information Act 2013 provides some accountability mechanisms. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms (e.g., dedicated ID tribunals or courts, specific rights-of-appeal processes for biometric data disputes) have been identified in available sources. Value set to 2 (Yes but not ID-specific).
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources; neither explicitly discusses judicial review of ID authority decisions. NCRA/about describes the Authority's establishment and mandate under the NCR Act 2016; Dubawa covers the mandatory ID card rollout. No ID-specific judicial mechanism (e.g. dedicated tribunal or statutory right of appeal to courts) was found in any source reviewed. The score rests on the general principle that NCRA, as a statutory public body, is subject to ordinary judicial review under Sierra Leone's common-law court system, rather than on direct source confirmation. Flagged for human review given the weak direct sourcing for the specific score value.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's ordinary courts retain general jurisdiction to review the actions of public bodies, including the National Civil Registration Authority, under common-law administrative law principles. No dedicated ID-specific judicial or appeal mechanism has been identified.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Sierra Leone has a fully integrated CRVS and ID management system under the NCRA. Civil registration of births, deaths, marriages, divorces, and adoptions is integrated with the national ID and NIN assignment in a single system. The NCRA ID4Africa 2024 presentation describes: 'Integrated CRVS & ID Management System serves as one-stop-shop for all Civil Registration, Vital Statistics & ID Management services.' NIN is assigned from birth, and deaths trigger NIN retirement. Full integration achieved.
revision_notes: Fetched cited sources (biometricupdate.com livecast article also reviewed). ID4Africa 2024 presentation explicitly confirms an 'Integrated Civil Registration Vital Statistics & ID Management System' serving as a one-stop-shop, with the NIN assigned from birth and linked to CRVS events. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone operates a fully integrated Civil Registration, Vital Statistics and ID Management system under the NCRA, in which civil registration of births, deaths, marriages, divorces and adoptions is combined with National Identification Number (NIN) assignment in a single platform, serving as a one-stop-shop for identity and vital events services.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing is partially formalized through bilateral MOUs and Data Sharing Agreements between NCRA and specific institutions. NCRA signed a Data Sharing Agreement with SLRSA (Oct 2023) and MOUs with commercial banks for eKYC. The NCR Act 2016 Section 25(e) provides the legal basis for data provision to authorized ministries. However, no comprehensive, publicly available national data sharing framework exists (noted as a gap by World Bank 2025). Data sharing rules are partially available—governed case-by-case by bilateral agreements.
revision_notes: The originally cited NCRA-SLRSA data sharing agreement page could not be read cleanly (returned corrupted/binary content on fetch) but is a genuine NCRA URL, so treated as unverifiable rather than dead. The NCR Act 2016 (fetched) contains specific statutory provisions permitting disclosure of registration data to named bodies (e.g. Ministry of Defence, National Electoral Commission) but no comprehensive publicly available data-sharing framework. The World Bank (Dec 2025) explicitly notes 'the lack of a data protection framework and siloed systems undermine safe ID use.' As of April 2026, Sierra Leone's Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill has only just been approved by Cabinet and is not yet enacted, confirming that data sharing remains governed by ad hoc statutory provisions and bilateral MOUs rather than a comprehensive published framework. Score confirmed as partially available; year updated to reflect the freshest evidence.
revised_comments: Data sharing by the National Civil Registration Authority is governed by specific statutory provisions in the National Civil Registration Act 2016 permitting disclosure to named institutions, together with bilateral memoranda of understanding and data-sharing agreements (for example with the Sierra Leone Road Safety Authority and commercial banks for eKYC). A comprehensive, publicly available national data protection and data-sharing framework does not yet exist: a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill was approved by Cabinet in April 2026 and awaits enactment by Parliament.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: The National Civil Registration Act 2016 is specific to civil registration and national identity management, establishing the NCRA with a mandate covering NIN issuance, biometric registration, and digital identity. The 2022 Cabinet Directive and Parliamentary ratification tied NIN to access for financial, telecom, social, and public services. The Electronic Transactions Act 2023 also covers digital ID-related regulations. These constitute a digital ID-specific regulatory framework.
revision_notes: Fetched cited and additional sources. The NCR Act 2016 is general civil registration/identification legislation rather than digital-ID-specific regulation; however, the 2022 Cabinet Directive (ratified by Parliament) specifically mandates NIN/digital ID linkage across financial, telecom, education, immigration and other services, which functions as digital-ID-specific policy. Evidence is a reasonable but not unambiguous match to the variable definition ('regulation... beyond general identification legislation'); retained at Yes=2 given the Cabinet Directive, but the distinction from general ID law is not sharply drawn in available sources.
revised_comments: Beyond the general National Civil Registration Act 2016, a Cabinet Directive ratified by Parliament in March 2022 specifically mandates linkage of the National Identification Number to access to financial services, education, healthcare, SIM registration, immigration, employment and other public services, constituting a digital-ID-specific policy layer on top of the underlying civil registration legislation.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The NIN and NCRA ID card are legally recognized as the primary source of personal identification in Sierra Leone. The NCR Act 2016 establishes the NCRA ID card as the definitive identity credential. A Cabinet Directive ratified by Parliament in March 2022 mandates the NIN as prerequisite for accessing financial services, education, healthcare, SIM registration, immigration, employment, and public services. From January 2025, all other forms of ID (voter card, etc.) are no longer accepted as primary identification.
revision_notes: Fetched all three cited sources; all state directly that the NCRA ID card bearing the NIN is 'by law the primary source of personal identification in Sierra Leone.' Score strongly confirmed.
revised_comments: The National Identification Number (NIN) and accompanying NCRA identity card are recognised in law as the primary source of personal identification in Sierra Leone. A Cabinet Directive ratified by Parliament in March 2022 mandates NIN possession for access to financial services, education, healthcare, SIM registration, immigration, employment and public services, with enforcement strengthened from January 2025.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The National Civil Registration Act 2016 establishes the NCRA and provides the legal basis for compulsory registration of all residents and issuance of multipurpose ID cards. revision_notes: Fetched the full text of the National Civil Registration Act 2016, confirming it establishes the NCRA, mandates compulsory registration of citizens and non-citizens, and provides for issuance of multipurpose identity cards and NINs. Score strongly confirmed.
revised_comments: The National Civil Registration Act 2016 establishes the National Civil Registration Authority and provides the legal basis for compulsory registration of all residents, assignment of National Identification Numbers, and issuance of multipurpose identity cards. A 2022 Cabinet Directive ratified by Parliament further mandates NIN linkage for access to public and private services.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance has partial oversight over the NCRA's budget and the national ID system. A Cabinet Directive (2022) was ratified by Parliament, with the Ministry of Finance noted as having compliance oversight under the securitized ID card rollout. The NCRA falls under the general government expenditure framework reviewed by the Ministry of Finance. No evidence of full, dedicated Ministry of Finance-led oversight specific to the ID system; the arrangement is partial, with NCRA having significant operational autonomy.
revision_notes: The originally cited Facebook post (a 2022 press conference held at the Ministry of Finance conference hall) does not itself establish an oversight relationship and is weak evidence. A stronger primary source was located and fetched: the National Civil Registration Act 2016 provides that the NCRA Board includes the Financial Secretary, Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (s.4(2)(d)), that the Board oversees 'sound and proper financial management' of the Authority, that NCRA's budget is financed by parliamentary appropriation and must be audited by the Auditor-General, and that NCRA submits an annual report including audited accounts to 'the Minister'. This confirms Ministry of Finance representation and budgetary accountability but not direct, full MoF control over NCRA's budget -- consistent with 'partial oversight' (2). Score confirmed and re-sourced.
revised_comments: The Ministry of Finance has partial oversight of the National Civil Registration Authority's financing: the Financial Secretary of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development sits on the NCRA Board, which is responsible for the Authority's sound financial management, and NCRA's budget is subject to parliamentary appropriation and annual audit by the Auditor-General. The Authority nonetheless retains its own dedicated revenue streams and day-to-day budgetary management.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The NCRA collects 10 fingerprints, 1 facial photograph, and 1 signature during biometric civil registration. The ID4Africa 2024 presentation by NCRA explicitly states: 'Biometric Data: 10 Fingerprint, 1 face, 1 Signature'. This meets the Facial/Iris level (scale value 3) as both fingerprints and facial recognition are used.
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources. ID4Africa 2024 presentation states biometric data collected is '10 Fingerprint, 1 face, 1 Signature'; NCRA registration page confirms fingerprints and photograph are captured. Facial biometric capture confirms the Facial/Iris tier (3) rather than fingerprints-only (2). Score confirmed.
revised_comments: The NCRA collects ten fingerprints, one facial photograph and a signature during biometric civil registration, as confirmed in NCRA's ID4Africa AGM 2024 presentation and its registration process documentation.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: NCRA established a Tier III Data Center for local storage of all registration data. The system is fully digital: 'Upgraded integrated eCRVS System for Births, Deaths, Marriage, Divorce, Adoption events registration' and 'Established Tier III Data Center. Data stored locally for security and country ownership.' Over 80% of services are digitized (NCRA 2025). Historic paper records are being digitized (30% linked as of 2025).
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources. ID4Africa 2024 confirms an upgraded integrated eCRVS system and a Tier III data centre storing all registration data electronically; all registrations since the 2016/17 rollout have been captured digitally via VIU biometric kits. Biometric Update (June 2025) reports 80% of NCRA services are digitised and confirms an ongoing programme to digitise legacy paper records, of which about 30% have been linked to the digital system as of mid-2025 (70% remaining). Current registration data is fully digital; historic pre-2016 paper records are only partially digitised, which is a genuine caveat but does not change the overall 'Digital' classification of the operating system. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Identity records are stored in an electronic Integrated CRVS and ID Management System hosted on a dedicated Tier III data centre. All registrations since the system's 2016/17 rollout are captured digitally via biometric enrolment kits, and as of mid-2025 around 80% of NCRA services were digitised. Digitisation of historic pre-2016 paper records is ongoing, with roughly 30% linked to the digital system to date.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The NIN registration itself is free. However, the physical eID card carries a fee: NLe 140 (~$7 USD) for nationals aged 12+, with additional NLe 5 application fee. Non-national cards cost NLe 2,000 (~$100 USD). The World Bank (Dec 2025) notes: 'For most Sierra Leoneans living on less than $2.15 a day, the $6–7 fee keeps ID cards out of reach.' The credential (physical card) is NOT free; scale value 1 (No, i.e., there is a cost) applies.
revision_notes: Fetched all cited sources. NCRA's own fee schedule confirms a NLe140 fee for national ID cards (aged 12+), NLe5 application fee, NLe240-400 for ECOWAS cards, and NLe2,000 for non-national cards. World Bank (Dec 2025) confirms the $6-7 fee remains a barrier to card uptake for most Sierra Leoneans. Biometric Update (Jan 2023) documents the fee hike history. NIN registration itself is free but the physical eID card carries a fee. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Registration for a National Identification Number is free, but the physical eID card is not: it costs NLe140 (plus a NLe5 application fee) for nationals aged 12 and above, NLe240-400 for ECOWAS cards, and NLe2,000 for non-national cards. The World Bank notes that this roughly $6-7 fee keeps ID cards out of reach for most Sierra Leoneans living on less than $2.15 a day, contributing to card uptake of under half a million as of 2024 despite around 6.4 million people holding a NIN.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Sierra Leone issues ECOWAS National Biometric ID Cards (ENBIC) compliant with ECOWAS standards, providing some regional recognition. Sierra Leone is listed among the ECOWAS countries that have deployed the ENBIC (one of the first seven: Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Ghana, Benin, The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Nigeria). The ECOWAS ID card enables free movement within ECOWAS member states as a travel document. However, full formally interoperable cross-border authentication infrastructure is not yet in place. Scale value 2 (Some regional).
revision_notes: Fetched all cited sources. Kolaking (Nov 2025) confirms Sierra Leone is among the seven ECOWAS member states that have deployed the ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC), which functions as a regional travel document. This does not amount to formal cross-border interoperability of authentication infrastructure. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone issues an ECOWAS-compliant biometric ID card (ENBIC), and is one of seven ECOWAS member states (with Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Ghana, Benin, The Gambia and Nigeria) to have deployed it as of late 2025. The card functions as a regional travel document, providing recognition in some regional contexts, though full cross-border interoperability of identity authentication has not been established.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Registration is open from birth (age 0) for all residents. The NCRA website states: 'Registration can be done for everyone aged 0 year and above.' The ID4Africa 2024 presentation confirms ~2.5 million children under 18 registered. NIN is assigned at registration to children, citizens, and non-citizens. Scale value 5 (<1, i.e., from birth/age 0) applies.
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources. NCRA's registration process page states directly: 'Registration can be done for everyone aged 0 year and above.' ID4Africa 2024 confirms roughly 2.5 million children under 18 are registered. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Registration for a National Identification Number is open from birth: the NCRA states that registration can be done for everyone aged zero years and above, and around 2.5 million children under 18 are already registered.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Registration is mandatory for all residents under the NCR Act 2016: 'All Citizens and Non-Citizens resident in Sierra Leone are Mandated by law (NCR Act 2016) to register with the NCRA.' From January 2025, enforcement was strengthened with security sector checks for ID cards. Both nationals and non-nationals are required to register. Scale value 3 (Mandatory for all) applies.
revision_notes: Fetched all cited sources. NCRA registration page states registration is mandated by law (NCR Act 2016) for all citizens and non-citizens resident in Sierra Leone. Forumnews-sl and Dubawa (both Dec 2024) confirm enforcement was strengthened from January 2025 via security-sector ID checks. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Registration for a National Identification Number is mandatory by law (National Civil Registration Act 2016) for all citizens and non-citizens resident in Sierra Leone. Enforcement was strengthened from January 2025, with the security sector conducting ID checks at checkpoints and in communities nationwide.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: All non-nationals resident in Sierra Leone are mandated to register with the NCRA and obtain a Non-National ID Card. ECOWAS citizens are issued ECOWAS ID Cards; other foreign nationals are issued Non-National eID Cards. Diplomatic exemptions exist for the card fee but not for NIN registration. Coverage is universal for all residents regardless of nationality. Scale value 3 (All) applies.
revision_notes: Fetched all cited sources. NCRA's card categories page confirms Non-National ID Cards and ECOWAS ID Cards are issued to foreign residents, with diplomatic waivers only exempting the fee (not registration). Forumnews-sl confirms both citizens and non-citizens must comply with mandatory registration. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: All non-nationals resident in Sierra Leone, including ECOWAS citizens and other foreign nationals, are eligible and legally required to register with the NCRA. ECOWAS citizens receive ECOWAS-compliant ID cards, while other foreign nationals receive Non-National eID Cards; only diplomats with formal waivers are exempted from the card fee, not from NIN registration itself.
